definitions.explanation: The protective silk casing spun by silkworm larvae before they transform into moths. Also used for cocoons of other insects. Historically important in Japan as the basis of the silk industry.

examples.japanese: ⟦{蚕|かいこ}→蚕：21218_kaiko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{繭|まゆ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
⟦{白|しろ}い→白い：00587_shiroi⟧{繭|まゆ}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{絹糸|きぬいと}→絹糸：27626_kinuito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧とれる。
examples.english: Silk thread is obtained from white cocoons.

examples.japanese: ⟦かつて→かつて：10303_katsute⟧⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{地方|ちほう}→地方：02369_chihou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{繭|まゆ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{生産|せいさん}→生産：01444_seisan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{盛|さか}ん→盛ん：01239_sakan⟧だった。
examples.english: Cocoon production used to be thriving in this region.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Silk production (⟦{養蚕|ようさん}→養蚕：27720_yousan⟧) was a major industry in Japan from the Meiji era through the early 20th century. Many rural areas in central Japan, especially Gunma Prefecture, were known for raising silkworms and producing cocoons. The Tomioka Silk Mill ({富岡製糸場|とみおかせいしじょう}) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
